His hat is half unravelled; the wool trails back to his own pot.} {Tobias is nowhere to be seen.|A note on Gerald's empty pot says "BACK SOON, DO NOT LET HIM NEAR THE TOMATOES."|{season == "winter": He's shivering, defiantly.|The seedlings around him are wilting with alarm.}} Fix his hat and carry him home {You re-knit the hat with two pencils and great patience. Gerald lets you, then bites your thumb, which Tobias says means he loves you.|You lift him gently out of the teacup. He screams softly the whole way home and bites you once at the end, fondly.|You tie off the trailing wool and carry him home in your cupped hands. The bite is affectionate. It still stings.} Re-pot the seedlings he trampled {You leave Gerald where he is and save the seedlings he kicked out. He watches you work, screaming softly with approval.|You re-pot a row of uprooted seedlings and leave the teacup alone. Mandrakes are Tobias's department.|You patch up the damage around the fern and let Gerald keep his new home. It seems kinder than arguing with a mandrake.}
